doc: Query-semantics parity oracle (issue #1742).
This file is a DIFFERENT oracle from the physical sstabledump JSONL goldens
(`*-Data.db.jsonl`). The physical goldens enumerate every on-disk cell —
INCLUDING tombstones, deleted rows, and expired-but-uncompacted TTL cells.
Row-count/value parity against a physical dump therefore CANNOT catch a
read-time-reconciliation bug: when CQLite fails to reconcile, both sides still
contain the shadowed/expired rows and parity passes while a real Cassandra
SELECT diverges (issue #1741, the read-path P0 this oracle guards against
regressing).
Each case below records the POST-RECONCILIATION result set a real Cassandra
`SELECT` returns for a canonical query, evaluated at a PINNED `now`
(`pinned_now_secs`, epoch seconds) so TTL expiry is deterministic and never
wall-clock-flaky. The reader honors the pin via the debug-only
`CQLITE_TTL_NOW_OVERRIDE_SECS` seam (see `now_clock.rs`).
`physical_row_count` is the count of `type == "row"` entries in the committed
sstabledump golden — an anti-empty-pass sanity check AND (where it exceeds
`expected_rows.len()`) a direct demonstration of the physical-vs-semantic gap
this oracle exists to close.
`physical_static_only_partitions` (additive-optional, default 0; issue #3095)
is the count of golden partitions holding a `static_block` and NO `row` entry.
Cassandra returns exactly ONE result row for each such partition, and that row
has no physical `row` behind it — so it is the ONLY way a correct semantic
result may legitimately EXCEED `physical_row_count`. Both lanes re-derive the
count from the golden and assert this declaration, so the allowance can never
be inflated to mask an over-emitting read path.
`ddl` (additive-optional) is the keyspace-qualified `CREATE TABLE` the FLIGHT
lane's ticket must carry, required for any table whose shape differs from the
`(id int, ck int, v text, PRIMARY KEY (id, ck))` shape shared by every table
in `compaction-tombstone-ttl-parity.cql` (e.g. a `static` column).
Consumed by cqlite-core/tests/query_semantics_oracle_parity.rs.

note: All three fixtures below are REAL Apache Cassandra 5.0.2 SSTables committed
to the repo (test-data/datasets/sstables/test_compaction_tombstone_ttl/**),
with provenance already tracked in test-data/cassandra-parity-manifest.yml
(scenarios cass.compaction.*shadow_row_delete / *ttl_expired_live /
*rt_cross_gen). They are post-major-compaction (nb-3-big) fixtures and still
present the physical-vs-semantic divergence (a physical dump enumerates the
surviving row/RT/expired markers that a SELECT hides).
GAP (issue #1742 AC2): a dedicated SINGLE-generation (pre-compaction) fixture
carrying coexisting partition-deletion + older LIVE rows, a range tombstone
with a LIVE row INSIDE its bounds, and an expired TTL cell whose VALUE is
still on disk requires generating uncompacted SSTables from a live Cassandra
container (autocompaction disabled, single flush). Docker/Cassandra was not
available in the implementing sandbox, so no such fixture is added here.
Tracked for real-Cassandra regeneration in the issue #1742 follow-up.

cases.ddl: CREATE TABLE test_deltas.static_with_rows (pk int, ck int, static_col text static, row_col text, PRIMARY KEY (pk, ck))
cases.query: SELECT pk, ck, static_col, row_col FROM test_deltas.static_with_rows
cases.pinned_now_note: 2027-01-15T08:00:00Z — after every write in the fixture. It carries no TTL, tombstone or deletion of any kind, so the pin only removes wall-clock nondeterminism (#2642); it never selects between rows.
note: Issue #3095 (STATIC-column SELECT semantics). THE case a physical dump
structurally cannot express, in both directions:
* a `static_block` in the golden is NOT a result row, yet its value must
appear on EVERY clustering row of its partition — so a physical-dump
comparison passes while `SELECT` returns a phantom `ck = null` row per
static-bearing partition AND a null static column on every real row
(exactly the defect #3095 found: 16 rows where Cassandra returns 13);
* conversely a partition holding ONLY a static row (`pk = 99` here: a
`static_block` and no `row` entry) has ZERO physical rows but returns
ONE result row — so `physical_static_only_partitions` (1) is the amount
by which the semantic result LEGITIMATELY exceeds `physical_row_count`.
Both lanes re-derive that count from the committed golden and assert it,
so it can never be inflated to mask an over-emitting read path.
Oracle derivation — Cassandra 5.0.8 `SelectStatement.processPartition()`:
the static row is fetched OUT OF BAND via `partition.staticRow()`
(`db/rows/BaseRowIterator.java`), so `partition.hasNext()` counts clustering
rows only; with N > 0 clustering rows the loop emits N rows and fills every
`case STATIC:` slot from that partition-level static row; with ZERO
clustering rows it emits exactly one row (clustering + REGULAR columns null
via `default: result.add((ByteBuffer) null)`) and returns.
Fixture: `test_deltas.static_with_rows` is a real Apache Cassandra 5.0.2
container flush (`test-data/scripts/generate-deltas.sh`, autocompaction
disabled, single `nodetool flush`) with a COMMITTED `Data.db` + golden. A
CQLite-written round trip could not serve as the oracle here: it is
invariant to a uniform assembly error and is confounded by the write-side
#1074 (statics placed into the clustering row) — see #3042.

No TTL; pin fixed for determinism. A range tombstone covers clustering [10,25]; the live rows sit at ck=5 and ck=30 (OUTSIDE the RT), so both survive — this pins that the RT open/close markers are skipped and do not wrongly shadow rows outside their bounds. A LIVE-row-INSIDE-RT case needs the single-gen fixture noted in provenance.gap.

cases.query: SELECT pk, ck FROM test_da.wide_table WHERE pk = 1 AND ck >= 100 AND ck < 110
cases.pinned_now_note: 2027-01-15T08:00:00Z. This fixture carries no TTL, tombstone or deletion of any kind (every row is unconditionally live at any now), so the pin only removes wall-clock nondeterminism from the lane; it never selects between rows.
note: Issue #3002 (BTI Rows.db row-index root base + leading OSS50 NEXT_COMPONENT).
A BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVATION oracle for the BTI clustering-slice read path
(`scan_single_partition_clustering` -> `resolve_clustering_seek_window` ->
`bti_clustering_row_window`): the two compensating defects cancelled on this
fixture, so the semantic result set must be IDENTICAL before and after removing
the compensation. A change here is a regression, not a semantic update.
Oracle derivation: test_da/wide_table is a real Apache Cassandra 5.0 `da` (BTI)
SSTable whose committed sstabledump golden (da-2-bti-Data.db.jsonl) holds 900
physical rows (3 partitions x ck=0..299) with NO tombstone/TTL/deletion marker,
so physical == semantic here: the expected result set is exactly the golden's
pk=1 rows with 100 <= ck < 110, read off the golden rather than hand-authored.
flight_lane=false: the Flight `do_get` ticket surface is a whole-table projection
scan with no WHERE clause, so a partition + clustering-slice query is not
expressible on that lane (see cqlite-flight/tests/query_semantics_flight_parity.rs).

note: Issue #3094: a DELETED CELL must read as NULL, never surface a raw tombstone.
THE CELL-TOMBSTONE SHAPE ON CASSANDRA-WRITTEN BYTES. test_tomb
static_with_tombstones is a real Apache Cassandra 5.0 `nb` SSTable (single
flush), committed to the repo with provenance in
test-data/cassandra-parity-manifest.yml. Its committed sstabledump golden
(nb-1-big-Data.db.jsonl) enumerates, in partition pk=1:
* a STATIC BLOCK holding ONE live cell, stat_col='surviving_static'
(tstamp 2021-01-01, no deletion_info, no TTL)
* ck=1 - live liveness marker + live row_col='row_1'
* ck=2 - a ROW DELETION (marked_deleted 2021-01-02), zero cells
* ck=3 - a LIVE liveness marker (tstamp 2021-01-01) whose ONLY regular
cell, row_col, is a SIMPLE CELL TOMBSTONE (tstamp 2021-01-02)
* a RANGE TOMBSTONE bound pair covering [ck=4, ck=5] (marked_deleted
2021-01-02); no data rows lie inside it in this fixture
* ck=6 - live liveness marker + live row_col='row_6'
CASSANDRA 5.0.8 DERIVATION of the expected result set, per `ck` (every
expectation below is read off the golden above plus the pinned
cassandra-5.0.8 sources named here - never off CQLite's own output). The
client-visible result is what `db/transform/Filter.java` yields:
applyToRow() = `row.purge(DeletionPurger.PURGE_ALL, nowInSec,
enforceStrictLiveness)`, and applyToMarker() returns null.
* ck=1 -> RETURNED, row_col='row_1'. No tombstone and no expiring cell,
so BTreeRow.purge()'s `!hasDeletion(nowInSec)` short-circuit
returns the row unchanged.
* ck=2 -> ABSENT. Its primaryKeyLivenessInfo is EMPTY (the golden shows
deletion_info and no liveness_info) and it carries zero cells;
PURGE_ALL strips the row deletion to Deletion.LIVE, so
BTreeRow.update()'s `info.isEmpty() && deletion.isLive() &&
BTree.isEmpty(newTree)` returns NULL and the row is dropped.
This holds independently of enforceStrictLiveness.
* ck=3 -> RETURNED with row_col NULL. Its liveness marker is live (no
TTL), so shouldPurge(LivenessInfo, nowInSec) is false and the
marker is kept; its only cell is a tombstone, which
AbstractCell.purge() maps to null. update() therefore does NOT
return null (info is non-empty) and yields a row with zero
cells, which SelectStatement.processPartition() renders as
`result.add(row.getColumnData(def) /* null */, nowInSec)` = NULL.
* ck=4, ck=5 -> ABSENT. The generator inserted them at T_GEN1 and range-
deleted them at T_GEN2 before the single flush, so the memtable
merge left NO `row` entry on disk - only the RangeTombstone
bound pair, and Filter.applyToMarker() returns null, so markers
are never client-visible.
* ck=6 -> RETURNED, row_col='row_6' (same short-circuit as ck=1).
* stat_col='surviving_static' on ALL THREE returned rows, ck=3
INCLUDED. processPartition() captures `Row staticRow =
partition.staticRow()` ONCE per partition and, inside its
per-row loop, serves `case STATIC: result.add(
staticRow.getColumnData(def), nowInSec)` - so the static row
is a SEPARATE object attached to every emitted clustering row,
never read from that row's own (here purged) cells. The static
row itself survives Filter.applyToStatic(): it is non-empty,
and purge()'s `!hasDeletion(nowInSec)` short-circuit returns it
unchanged because its one cell is live.
So the SELECT returns 3 rows (ck = 1, 3, 6), one of them with
row_col = null and all three with stat_col = 'surviving_static', while
the physical dump shows 4 `type: row` entries.
This is exactly the divergence a physical-dump oracle CANNOT catch: the
golden enumerates the cell tombstone, so parity against it stays green
while a real SELECT diverges. Before #3094 the deleted cell reached the row
carrier as Value::Tombstone(CellTombstone) and the fail-closed Arrow
encoder (#1485) errored the WHOLE Flight do_get stream.
SCOPE OF THE QUERY (why the FULL `WHERE pk = 1` slice, and why stat_col
IS now projected). Issue #3164 RETIRED the `ck >= 3` bound this case
originally carried. When #3094 added the case, the row-tombstoned ck=2 was
wrongly surfacing as an all-null row: on the single-generation read path
`merge_static_cells` injected the live stat_col into ck=2 BEFORE
`build_display_row` ran, so `has_data_cell` was true and the row was
emitted as data instead of a filtered tombstone MARKER. The bound existed
so this case could own the CELL-TOMBSTONE property alone and never encode
that phantom row as expected behaviour. That mechanism is FIXED - statics
are excluded from the row-tombstone decision (PR #3141, issue #3095) and
the rule is pinned at all three gated decode sites by PR #3159 (issue
#3121, cqlite-core/tests/issue_3121_static_row_tombstone_no_phantom.rs) -
so the bound is now pure under-coverage and the case asserts the whole
partition, ck=2's ABSENCE included. Should ck=2 ever reappear as an
all-null row, those three tests are the ones to consult first.
stat_col is PROJECTED, which is the point of a case named
static_with_tombstones: it asserts that the live static cell attaches to
every surviving row of a tombstone-riddled partition - ck=3 included,
where the row's own regular cell was purged. #3164 considered omitting it
on the grounds that the static read shape is a tracked divergence, but
BypassReason::StaticColumns lives in cqlite-flight/src/bypass.rs and is a
property of the FLIGHT single-SSTable bypass predicate; nothing in
cqlite-core consults it, and this case is flight_lane=false, so it does
not gate this lane. The slice keeps TWO live control rows (ck=1,
row_col='row_1' and ck=6, row_col='row_6') in the same result set, so the
ck=3 null cannot pass vacuously as a blanket loss of row_col, and stat_col
is asserted non-null on all three so a blanket loss of the static cell
cannot pass either.
flight_lane=false: the Flight `do_get` ticket surface is a whole-table
projection scan with no WHERE clause, so even this partition-restricted
slice is not expressible on that lane. The Flight `do_get` arms for this
property are
covered instead by cqlite-flight/tests/issue_3094_cell_tombstone_null.rs
(both forced arms) and by the re-enabled ck=5 cell-tombstone shape in
cqlite-flight/tests/issue_3058_forced_path_differential.rs.
